name: Mepitiostane (Thioderon)

lead: Mepitiostane (Thioderon) is an oral steroid the body converts into epitiostanol, combining antiestrogen activity with weak anabolic and androgenic activity. Bodybuilders discuss it for a drier, leaner contest look.

Epitiostanol binds the estrogen receptor as an antagonist and the androgen receptor as an agonist, which is the basis for the less-water, harder-muscle idea. In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia in kidney failure, with a phase III trial against medroxyprogesterone acetate in breast cancer. Animal studies show the intact molecule travels via intestinal lymph, letting part of the dose bypass first-pass liver metabolism. No human study has tested it for appearance.

paras: It is an oral prescription drug in Japan. Physique use is based on discussion in bodybuilding circles rather than documented routines.

Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, such as acne, hirsutism and voice changes. It is prescription-only where sold, and sports authorities prohibit it; urine tests for its metabolites exist.

chain: Less water and fat, drier muscle look
angle.text: Mepitiostane is discussed for a drier, leaner look: it converts to epitiostanol, which blocks estrogen action and weakly activates androgen receptors. It is used medically in Japan for breast cancer and renal anemia; no appearance studies exist.

lead: Mepitiostane (brand name Thioderon) is an orally active synthetic steroid of the dihydrotestosterone group that acts as an antiestrogen and a weak anabolic-androgenic steroid. It is a prodrug, meaning it is converted in the body to epitiostanol, the active compound. [1]

In Japan it has been marketed for breast cancer and for anemia associated with kidney failure. [1] Published clinical work includes a phase III comparison with medroxyprogesterone acetate in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer, a study in hemodialysis patients with ACE-inhibitor-related anemia, and a case report of a presumed meningioma that regressed during treatment. [2][3][4]

No published human study has examined mepitiostane for bodybuilding or other appearance goals. Interest in it comes from its classification as an anabolic-androgenic steroid and from its listing in anti-doping analytical literature. [5]

paras: Wikipedia states that mepitiostane is marketed in Japan as an antineoplastic agent for breast cancer and is also used for anemia in renal failure. [1]

A 1985 phase III trial compared oral high-dose medroxyprogesterone acetate with mepitiostane in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer. [2] A 1989 study in chronic hemodialysis patients examined whether adding mepitiostane prevented the worsening of anemia seen with ACE inhibitors such as captopril and enalapril. [3] A 2000 case report described regression of a presumed meningioma during treatment with the drug. [4]

Mepitiostane is the 1-methoxycyclopentyl ether of epitiostanol. After it is absorbed, it is converted to epitiostanol, which antagonizes the estrogen receptor and also has androgenic activity. Wikipedia compares its antiestrogen action to that of tamoxifen. [1]

Rat studies found that when mepitiostane was placed in the small intestine, about a third of the radioactivity appeared in thoracic duct lymph, mostly as unchanged drug carried in chylomicrons and VLDL. The portal blood fraction was extensively taken up by the liver. The authors concluded that lymphatic absorption lets mepitiostane avoid part of first-pass metabolism. [6]

Further rat work found that the extent of lymphatic absorption depended on the oily vehicle used, with long-chain triglycerides such as triolein and sesame oil giving the greatest uptake, and that bile also affected absorption. [7][8] Comparison with epitiostanol found that the prodrug was transferred into lymph far more than epitiostanol itself. [9]
Wikipedia reports a high rate of virilizing effects in women, including acne, hirsutism and voice changes. [1]

The World Anti-Doping Agency prohibits mepitiostane. A 2015 analytical study described a liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method to detect its urinary metabolites, epitiostanol sulfoxide and epitiostanol, for sports drug testing. [5]

No studies of mepitiostane for muscle gain, body composition or other appearance outcomes were found. Human studies concern disease settings: a phase III trial in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer against medroxyprogesterone acetate [2], a study of anemia in hemodialysis patients taking ACE inhibitors [3], and a single case report in a presumed meningioma [4].

timeline.event: A phase III trial compares mepitiostane with medroxyprogesterone acetate in advanced postmenopausal breast cancer. [2]
An LC-MS/MS method for urinary mepitiostane metabolites is published for doping control. [5]
